Sam: hi — quick onboarding q about PR hygiene. When should I squash commits vs keep them? also accidentally pushed a debug config with an API key (rotated now)  how do I clean history safely before asking for reviews?
Nina: welcome Sam! usual rule: squash related incremental commits into a single logical commit for readability (use size/XS or size/S for small changes). keep separate commits when they represent distinct logical steps (e.g., "add feature X" + "add tests for X").
Jorge: for the secret: good you rotated the key. remove the secret from the branch history before merging. recommended flow:
```bash
# interactive rebase to squash/remove the bad commit
git checkout -b fix/remove-secret
git rebase -i main
# mark the offending commit as edit, then remove the secret from the files, git add, git commit --amend, git rebase --continue
# force-push after cleaning history (only to your feature branch):
git push --force-with-lease origin fix/remove-secret
```
Sam: thanks. do we have any automation that detects secrets?
devops-bot: secret-scan: scanned on push WARNING potential secret found in commit 3a4f2b. Please rotate and remove from history. More info: https://redwood.internal/security/secret-scanning
Nina: we also use pre-merge scans in CI. if you see devops-bot warnings, fix locally and push; then comment "fixed" so reviewers know.
Jorge: about squashing: if you're doing simple refactors or tiny bugfixes, squash into one commit with a clear subject line. If reviewers want to preserve granular history for future bisects, keep commits but tidy up messages (imperative mood). PR title should be imperative: "Remove debug config and rotate secret". PR description: short summary + testing steps + mention of any fallout (e.g., "rotated key, no consumer changes").
Sam: what about commit message format? we have conventional commits or the team uses small variants?
Nina: we prefer conventional-ish but not strict. good example: "fix(config): remove debug key from infra config" or "chore(deps): bump x". For user-visible changes, include a brief scope and a one-line summary, optional body with rationale.
Jorge: CI checks to expect: lint, unit tests, secret-scan, build-image. If you touch Dockerfiles or runtime containers, add @infra-team as reviewer. Also tag PR with labels: size/XS|S, chore|fix|feat, and mark "security" if it was a secret incident.
ci-bot: CI started for fix/remove-secret — lint: pass, tests: running, secret-scan: pending.
Sam: should I request reviewers or let CODEOWNERS handle it?
Nina: request 1 reviewer when it's a small internal change. For infra/runtime or anything touching deploy pipelines request 2 and ping infra. CODEOWNERS will auto-add required owners but manual pings speed up reviews.
Jorge: final nit on squashing: when force-pushing after history rewrite, always use --force-with-lease and include a comment in the PR like "rebased to remove secret, force-pushed" so reviewers know history changed.
Sam: got it, thanks! i'll clean the branch, force-with-lease, push, and then request Nina for a quick review. :)
Nina: welcome aboard — ping if CI flags anything. :tada:
